question.text: A uniform heavy rod of weight <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>,</mo></math> cross-sectional area <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>100</mn><msup><mrow><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></mrow><mn>2</mn></msup></math> and length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> is hanging from a fixed support. Young modulus of the material of the rod is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>11</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup><mo>.</mo></math> Neglecting the lateral contraction, find the elongation of rod due to its own weight:

solution.text:
Elongation due to self weight,
Wl2AY=10×0.22×2×1011×100×10-4=5×10-10 m
